summary:
**AstroShift: NASA Deep Space Outpost Commander**

AstroShift is a browser-based interactive STEM simulation developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The project transforms the challenges of deep-space exploration into an engaging mission-management experience for students aged 7–12. Players become space outpost commanders responsible for establishing and maintaining a sustainable human settlement on the Moon or Mars.

Through 15 mission days (Sols), players must manage interconnected life-support systems, including oxygen, water, electricity, food production, radiation protection, and crew health. They also operate autonomous rovers, experience realistic communication delays, respond to dynamic space hazards, and make strategic decisions with immediate and long-term consequences.

AstroShift addresses the challenge by turning complex aerospace engineering concepts into accessible, interactive learning experiences rather than passive educational content.

Its importance lies in helping young learners develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, resource-management skills, and an understanding of the real engineering challenges involved in sustainable human space exploration.

The experience includes bilingual Arabic and English support, child-friendly educational explanations, and an advanced Mission Control mode that introduces authentic scientific measurements and engineering concepts.

AstroShift: NASA Deep Space Outpost Commander

AstroShift is a browser-based interactive STEM simulation developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The project transforms the challenges of deep-space exploration into an engaging mission-management experience for students aged 7–12. Players become space outpost commanders responsible for establishing and maintaining a sustainable human settlement on the Moon or Mars.

Through 15 mission days (Sols), players must manage interconnected life-support systems, including oxygen, water, electricity, food production, radiation protection, and crew health. They also operate autonomous rovers, experience realistic communication delays, respond to dynamic space hazards, and make strategic decisions with immediate and long-term consequences.

AstroShift addresses the challenge by turning complex aerospace engineering concepts into accessible, interactive learning experiences rather than passive educational content.

Project Overview

AstroShift is an interactive, browser-based space mission command simulator designed to teach students the scientific and engineering challenges of establishing sustainable human outposts beyond Earth.

Players assume the role of mission commanders and manage a lunar or Martian settlement throughout a 15-Sol campaign.

How the Project Works

The simulation consists of interconnected systems:

  1. Life Support Management: Players monitor oxygen consumption, water recovery, cabin pressure, and environmental conditions to maintain crew survival.
  2. Power Management: Players balance solar energy generation, battery storage, electrical consumption, and the power requirements of different outpost modules.
  3. Food Production: An interactive hydroponic agriculture system simulates crop growth, irrigation, harvesting, and food sustainability.
  4. Radiation Protection: Players monitor radiation exposure and make decisions involving protective shielding, emergency shelters, and solar storm preparation.
  5. Planetary Exploration: Players experience different environmental conditions on the Moon and Mars, including gravity, temperature, atmospheric pressure, and surface hazards.
  6. Autonomous Rover Operations: Players dispatch exploration commands and experience realistic communication delays, autonomous rover behavior, and signal blackouts.
  7. Dynamic Events and Decision Making: Randomized space weather events, equipment failures, and environmental hazards create interconnected challenges with immediate and delayed consequences.
  8. Educational Feedback: After important decisions, the game explains what happened, why it happened, the scientific principles involved, and how the scenario connects to real space missions.
  9. Mission Evaluation: At the end of the campaign, players receive performance grades, achievements, and detailed mission debriefings based on their decisions.

Educational Benefits and Goals

  • Introduce students to aerospace engineering and planetary science.
  • Demonstrate the importance of sustainable resource management.
  • Explain real-world space exploration constraints.
  • Develop critical thinking and strategic decision-making.
  • Connect scientific theory with interactive experimentation.
  • Make advanced STEM concepts accessible to younger learners.

Technology Stack and Development Tools

  • Frontend Framework: React 19.
  • Programming Languages: TypeScript and JavaScript.
  • Build Tool: Vite.
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS v4.
  • Icons: Lucide React.
  • Visual Effects: Canvas Confetti.
  • Audio: Web Audio API.
  • Data Persistence: Browser LocalStorage.
  • Testing: Node.js and automated verification scripts.
  • Development Environment: Modern web development tools and AI-assisted coding tools.

Platform and Hardware

AstroShift is designed to run directly in a modern web browser without requiring installation or specialized hardware. A standard computer with an internet connection is sufficient for accessing its online scientific resources.
